name: Divisero – Multicurrency for WooCommerce
author: ProPluginsLab

sections.description:
Divisero lets your WooCommerce store show prices in your shopper’s own currency and take payment in that currency, while your books stay in your store currency. Every feature on this page is in the free plugin, with no limit on the number of currencies.

  • Product page: propluginslab.io
  • Documentation: docs.propluginslab.io/divisero-multicurrency-for-woocommerce
  • Support: propluginslab.io/support

The name comes from the Italian and Latin divisa, foreign currency.

What it does

  • Unlimited currencies from the full ISO 4217 list, plus custom currencies with your own code, name and symbol.
  • Display settings per currency: symbol, symbol position, decimals, thousand and decimal separators and flag. Zero decimal currencies such as JPY and KRW and three decimal currencies such as KWD and BHD work correctly everywhere, including the amounts sent to payment gateways.
  • Real checkout in the shopper’s currency. The cart, mini cart, shipping, coupons, taxes and the order are all in that currency. Or choose to charge in your store currency and show the converted prices as approximate.
  • Exchange rates entered by hand, or updated automatically from the European Central Bank on a schedule you pick (off until you switch it on). Add a markup per currency, and keep any rate fixed while the others update.
  • Rounding per currency: up, down or to the nearest step (0.01 to 10), and price endings such as .99, .95, .90 or 9. Rounding only touches converted prices.
  • Currency by country: geolocation with WooCommerce’s own MaxMind database or your CDN’s country header (Cloudflare, CloudFront), a country to currency map you can change, and an optional switch on the billing country at checkout.
  • A switcher everywhere: block, shortcode [divisero_switcher], classic widget, a Currency switcher item you place anywhere in Appearance, Menus, floating switcher and product page switcher, in four styles (dropdown, buttons, flags, compact), with a live preview. It works without JavaScript too.
  • Amounts and a converter in your content: [divisero_convert amount="25"] shows an amount in the shopper’s currency, [divisero_rates] a table of your exchange rates, and [divisero_converter] a small currency converter for shoppers.
  • Payment methods that can take the currency. Divisero knows which currencies more than 25 popular gateways accept, hides the ones that cannot take the shopper’s currency on the classic and the block checkout, and lets you set a fallback currency, so a shopper is told “PayPal cannot take payments in Kenyan shilling (KES). You will pay 54.20 USD instead.” before paying, never after a failed payment. Express buttons from Stripe (Apple Pay, Google Pay) and PayPal get the right currency or stay hidden.
  • Works with page caches out of the box. Divisero detects WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP-Optimize and 15 other caches, CDNs and hosts, and picks the mode that shows the right currency: one cached copy per currency where the cache supports it, or prices corrected in the browser right after a cached page loads. A “Test now” button checks it.
  • Setup wizard that detects your store, suggests currencies from your shipping zones and fills in sensible defaults.
  • Health check in plain words for currencies, rates, payment methods, cache, other currency plugins and geolocation, each with a fix or a link.
  • Import from other currency plugins: FOX Currency Switcher (WOOCS), CURCY, Aelia Currency Switcher, YayCurrency, WPML Multicurrency and Price Based on Country. Their settings are only read, never changed.
  • Accurate books. Every order stores its currency, the exchange rate used and its totals in your store currency, shown in a Currency details box on the order screen. The orders list has a currency column and filter.
  • Built for WooCommerce today: HPOS, the Cart and Checkout blocks, the Store API, the price filter block and widget, Action Scheduler and WooCommerce Subscriptions (renewals are charged in the currency of the first order).
  • Works with the ProPluginsLab plugins Mercenza, Plusero, Presentero, Inputo, Kitero, Anticipo, Affireo, Recovero, Storefold and Visuaro, and with Product Add-Ons, Name Your Price and Elementor.
  • Its own admin menu and built in documentation: Divisero has a menu of its own, with an item for every screen, the setup wizard, and a Documentation page that explains every option, with a search box.
  • Developer friendly: functions, filters and actions for everything, WP-CLI commands, settings export and import as JSON.
  • Private by default. Nothing is sent anywhere until you switch on automatic rates. No tracking, no statistics.

Divisero Pro

Divisero Pro adds fixed prices per product and currency with a bulk editor and CSV import, more exchange rate services with hourly updates, rate history and alerts, currency rules by language, role, customer and URL, SEO currency URLs, fixed coupon and shipping amounts per currency, multicurrency reports and admin orders in any currency. It is a one-time payment. See Divisero Pro.

External services

Divisero works without any outside service. It connects to one only when you switch it on, and it never sends anything about your shoppers.

European Central Bank (exchange rates)

The European Central Bank (ECB) publishes official reference exchange rates for about 30 currencies once every working day. Divisero uses them to update your exchange rates automatically.

When: only when you switch on “Update exchange rates automatically” under Divisero, Exchange rates (it is off by default) with the European Central Bank as the service. Divisero then downloads the rates on the schedule you pick (twice a day, once a day or once a week), when you press “Update now”, and once right after you add a currency while automatic updates are on.

What is sent: a plain request for the public file https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/eurofxref/eurofxref-daily.xml. No data about your store, your products, your orders or your shoppers is sent. As with any web request, the ECB sees the IP address of your server.

This service is provided by the European Central Bank:

  • Terms of use: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/using-our-site/disclaimer/html/index.en.html
  • Privacy policy: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/services/data-protection/html/index.en.html

Links to payment providers (nothing is sent)

The “Payment methods and currencies” grid shows a “Source” link for each payment method: the provider’s own page about the currencies it accepts (for example PayPal, Stripe, Square, Mollie, Klarna, Amazon Pay or Flutterwave). These are ordinary links that an administrator can click to read that page. Divisero never connects to these addresses and sends nothing to them.

Requests to your own site

The “Test now” button under Divisero, Cache loads one of your own product pages in each currency to check what your page cache returns. It only contacts your own site, and only when you press the button.

Divisero calls no geolocation service: the shopper’s country comes from WooCommerce’s MaxMind database stored on your own server, or from the country header your CDN already adds to each request. Flags are bundled with the plugin. The Documentation and Support links in the plugin are ordinary links to docs.propluginslab.io and propluginslab.io; nothing is sent to them.

sections.installation:
1. Install Divisero from the Plugins screen, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  3. The setup wizard opens on the next admin page. It takes about two minutes, and every choice can be changed later in the Divisero admin menu.
sections.faq:
Is there a limit on the number of currencies?

No. The free plugin supports every ISO 4217 currency and your own custom currencies, with no limit.

Do shoppers really pay in their currency?

Yes, by default. The order is created in the shopper’s currency and the gateway is asked to charge in it. If you prefer, choose “Shoppers pay in your store currency” under Checkout and payments: prices are then shown as approximate and the order is charged in your store currency.

What happens when a payment method cannot take a currency?

Divisero hides that payment method for that currency. If you set a fallback currency, the method stays visible and the shopper is told before paying that the order will be charged in the fallback currency. You can override what Divisero knows about any gateway under Checkout and payments.

Does it work with my page cache or CDN?

Yes. Divisero detects the cache and picks the right mode by itself. For WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache and WP Super Cache, one button on the Cache tab (it says exactly what changes) makes the cache keep a copy per currency. For every other cache, CDN or host cache, prices are corrected in the browser right after the page loads, with no cache rule to add. Cart, checkout and My Account are never cached by these tools.

Where does geolocation get the country?

From the MaxMind database you set up in WooCommerce, Settings, Integration, or from the country header your CDN adds, such as Cloudflare’s CF-IPCountry. No geolocation service is contacted.

Can I switch from another currency plugin?

Yes. Under Divisero, Tools, import the currencies, rates and country rules of FOX Currency Switcher (WOOCS), CURCY, Aelia, YayCurrency, WPML Multicurrency or Price Based on Country. Then deactivate the other plugin yourself; Divisero never switches plugins off.

Which plugins and themes were tested?

See the compatibility list on the Divisero product page. It lists only what was actually tested, with versions.

Is there a developer API?

Yes. Functions: divisero_get_active_currency(), divisero_get_default_currency(), divisero_get_base_currency(), divisero_get_enabled_currencies(), divisero_convert( $amount, $to, $from ), divisero_format_price( $amount, $currency ), divisero_get_rate( $currency ), divisero_switcher( $args ) and divisero_mark_product_converted( $product ). Filters include divisero_active_currency, divisero_currency_resolvers, divisero_convert_amount, divisero_rounded_amount, divisero_skip_conversion, divisero_product_fixed_price, divisero_gateway_supported_currencies, divisero_currency_from_country, divisero_cache_mode and divisero_switcher_html. Actions include divisero_currency_changed, divisero_rates_updated and divisero_order_currency_saved. WP-CLI: wp divisero currency list|add|update|delete, wp divisero rates list|update|set, wp divisero health and wp divisero import –from=.

Where are the JavaScript and CSS sources, and how do I rebuild them?

The human readable sources are in assets/src, next to package.json, package-lock.json and webpack.config.js. To rebuild the files in assets/build, run npm ci and then npm run build in the plugin folder. The flag images in assets/flags come from the country-flag-icons package (MIT licence); see assets/flags/LICENSE.txt.

What data does Divisero store about shoppers?

A cookie named divisero_currency with the currency code the shopper picked, and for logged in customers the same code in their account. Both are included in the WordPress personal data export and erase tools, and suggested text is added to your privacy policy guide.

What happens to my data when I delete the plugin?

By default your currencies, rates and settings are kept, so you can reinstall without losing anything. Switch off “Keep data when Divisero is deleted” under Settings to remove everything. Order currency records are accounting data, so they are only removed when you also tick “Also remove the currency records of orders”.
